passage: Hafsa, fourteen, was taller than most of her teachers, and her body had started changing well before anyone else's in Class Nine. In PE she hunched her shoulders, kept her jacket zipped in the heat and dawdled to be last onto the court. When a group of boys whispered and laughed as she ran, she walked off and sat by the water tank. Kiran Ma'am, the school counsellor, found her there. "I look so much older than everyone," Hafsa muttered. "They all stare." Kiran Ma'am sat beside her. "Bodies change on their own timetables. Some start early, some late, and all of it is normal. Your worth isn't measured by your body. And the staring and laughing is not okay. I'll speak to the PE teacher about it today." Hafsa unzipped her jacket an inch. "Can I come back to the court with you?"

qa.q: Where did Hafsa sit after walking off?
What was Hafsa feeling during PE?
qa.a: She felt self-conscious and awkward, hunching and keeping her jacket zipped to hide.

qa.q: Which parts of Kiran Ma'am's response helped, and why?
qa.a: Saying that timing varies and worth is not measured by the body, and acting on the teasing that same day, so Hafsa felt reassured and protected.

qa.q: What would change if the boys understood that timing varies?
qa.a: They might see Hafsa's body as simply normal and stop whispering, and she could run without feeling watched.

grounding: Shows a teenager who matured earlier than classmates feeling awkward and teased, and reassurance that timing varies and worth is not about the body.

passage:
Dear Yamini didi,
You said I could write about anything, so here goes. Everyone in my class has shot up this year. Rohit shaves. Even Faisal's voice has dropped. I'm still the shortest, my voice still squeaks, and in the changing room I keep my back to the wall. On Friday someone called me "little boy" in front of everyone, and I pretended to laugh. At home I stared in the mirror for ages, wondering if something is wrong with me. Our school nurse said timing is different for everyone, some people just start later, and if I'm ever worried she can arrange a check with the doctor. I want to believe her. Did you ever feel behind? How do you stop measuring yourself against everyone?
Divyansh

qa.q: What was Divyansh called on Friday?
How did Divyansh feel after being called that?
qa.a: He felt humiliated and left behind, pretending to laugh but later wondering if something was wrong with him.

qa.q: What could help Divyansh most right now?
qa.a: Trusting the nurse's reassurance that timing varies, keeping the option of a doctor's check if worried, and hearing that his worth is not measured by his height.

qa.q: How might Yamini respond to this letter?
qa.a: She would likely feel protective and reassure him that timing varies and that his value has nothing to do with his body.

grounding: Illustrates a later-developing teenager feeling teased and left behind, and reassurance that timing varies and worth is not measured by the body.
